questions.text: Which nervous system function gathers clues from inside and outside the body using the senses?
In the hot cocoa example, what is the 'motor output'?
options: Your fingers touch the hot cup
Your brain decides 'Ouch, that is too hot!'
Your arm muscles pull your hand away from the cup

questions.text: Where does integration (processing and deciding) take place?
options: In the brain and spinal cord

questions.text: The central nervous system (CNS) is made up of...
options: all nerves outside the brain and spinal cord
the brain and the spinal cord

questions.text: What does the peripheral nervous system (PNS) do?
options: Stores memories and makes major decisions
Carries messages between the CNS and the rest of the body

questions.text: Which branch of the PNS controls voluntary (conscious) movements?
Heartbeat, digestion, breathing, and sweating are controlled by the...
Which brain region thinks, learns, stores memory, and controls voluntary movement?
Which brain region controls balance, coordination, and posture?
Which part of the brain controls breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, and swallowing?
The hypothalamus controls...
options: body temperature, hunger, thirst, and hormones

questions.text: What are neurons?
options: Specialized messenger cells that pass electrical signals

questions.text: What do dendrites do?
options: Carry impulses away to target cells

questions.text: What is the job of the axon hillock?
options: To collect incoming signals and decide whether a nerve impulse fires

questions.text: What does the axon do?
options: Carries the electrical impulse away toward target cells

questions.text: What is the function of the myelin sheath?
options: It receives signals from other cells
It insulates the axon and speeds up signal transmission
It decides if an impulse fires

questions.text: What allows impulses to jump quickly along the axon ('saltatory conduction')?
What do synaptic terminals release across the synaptic gap?
Which system is known as the 'fight or flight' system?
What does the sympathetic system do to the pupils?
What does the parasympathetic system do to the heart rate?
options: Slows it down to the rest level

questions.text: What happens to digestion during 'fight or flight'?
options: It is inhibited and slows down

questions.text: Which gland releases adrenaline when the sympathetic system is active?
Which condition involves brain cell loss and abnormal protein clumps (plaques and tangles) that damage memory?
Which condition is caused by the gradual loss of brain cells that make dopamine?
Epilepsy is caused by...
options: sudden abnormal bursts of electrical activity across brain nerve cells

questions.text: In multiple sclerosis (MS), what does the immune system accidentally attack?
options: The protective myelin sheath around nerves

questions.text: Which habit helps prevent spinal cord injuries?
options: Wearing seatbelts and never diving into shallow water

questions.text: In a reflex arc, which part processes the signal in the spinal cord without waiting for the brain?
What is the first step of a reflex arc?
options: A sensory receptor detects a sudden stimulus

questions.text: In a reflex arc, which part carries the command out to the muscles?
Why is 8-10 hours of sleep good for the nervous system?
options: It makes neurons grow longer axons
It lets glial cells clear waste and helps build permanent memories
It stops all neuron activity forever
